2.text: studieth--meditateth. talk . . . mischief--Their expressed purposes are to do evil.

5.text: The general statement (Ecc 9:16, Ecc 9:18) is specially illustrated (compare Pro 21:22; Psa 144:1).

8.text: So called even if he fails to do evil.

10.text: Literally, "If thou fail in the day of straits (adversity), strait (or, small) is thy strength," which is then truly tested.

11.text: Neglect of known duty is sin (Jam 4:17). ready--literally, "bowing down" to be slain--that is, unjustly. God's retributive justice cannot be avoided by professed ignorance.

13.text: As delicious food whets the appetite, so should the rewards of wisdom excite us to seek it.

14.text: reward--literally, "after part," the proper result (compare Pro 23:18; Psa 37:37-38).

15.text: The plots of the wicked against the good, though partially, shall not be fully successful (Psa 37:24); while the wicked, falling under penal evil, find no help.

16.text: seven times--often, or many (Pro 6:16, Pro 6:31; Pro 9:1).

17.text: Yet let none rejoice over the fate of evildoers, lest God punish their wrong spirit by relieving the sufferer (compare Pro 17:5; Job 31:29).

20.text: candle--or, "prosperity"; it shall come to an end (Pro 13:9; Pro 20:20).

21.text: A warning against impiety and resistance to lawful rule (Rom 13:1-7; Pe1 2:17). meddle . . . change--(Compare Margin), literally, "mingle not yourself," avoid the society of restless persons.

22.text: their calamity, &c.--either what God and the king inflict, or what changers and their company suffer; better the first.

23.text: These . . . wise--literally, "are of the wise," as authors (compare "Psalms of David," Hebrew). "These" refers to the verses following, Pro 24:24-34. to have respect--literally, "to discern faces," show partiality,

24.text: of which an example is justifying the wicked, to which is opposed, rebuking him, which has a blessing.

26.text: kiss his lips--love and obey, do homage (Psa 2:12; Sol 8:1). right answer--literally, "plain words" (compare Pro 8:9), opposed to deceptive, or obscure.

27.text: Prepare . . . in the field--Secure, by diligence, a proper support, and then build; provide necessaries, then comforts, to which a house rather pertained, in a mild climate, permitting the use of tents.

28.text: Do not speak even truth needlessly against any, and never falsehood.

30.text: A striking picture of the effects of sloth.

32.text: From the folly of the sluggard learn wisdom (Pro 6:10-11). Next: Proverbs Chapter 25
